subject: physics
question_text: What is specific gas constant? Is it the same for all gases?

mark_split.label: Not the same for all gases, and why

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 11 Very Short Answer Question 11 (printed p.117). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: the specific gas constant r = R/M, where R is the universal gas constant (8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) and M is the molar mass of the gas; r is different for different gases because M differs, while R itself is the same for every gas (NCERT Class-11 kinetic theory).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition and formula
lines: The specific gas constant is the
universal gas constant taken per unit
R is the universal gas constant and M
is the molar mass of the gas.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write r = R/M with R and M both named.
steps.why: The universal gas constant R is the same for every gas, so dividing it by the molar mass M is what turns it into a constant that belongs to one particular gas.
common_mistakes: Writing r = RM instead of r = R/M.

recall.must_convey: That the specific gas constant is r = R/M, the universal gas constant per unit mass of the gas.
accept: universal gas constant per unit mass

steps.memory_tip: Small r is R divided by M — the universal constant shared out over one mole's mass.

steps.label: Not the same for all gases
lines: No, the specific gas constant is not
the same for all gases, because the
molar mass M is different for each
The universal gas constant R, unlike
r, is the same for every gas.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say r differs because M differs, while R itself does not.
steps.why: Since r = R/M and R is fixed, the only thing that can make r different from one gas to another is a different M — that is the whole reason r is called specific to a gas.
common_mistakes: Saying R itself changes from gas to gas. R is universal and fixed; only r changes.

recall.must_convey: That r is different for different gases because M differs, while R is the same for all gases.
accept: R is same for every gas

steps.memory_tip: R never changes; M does — so r changes with the gas, R does not.

insider_note: Two marks — the formula r = R/M naming both R and M, then the explicit statement that r differs across gases because M does, while R stays universal.
